run_1.first_failure: test_s5_stream_stops_gracefully_with_work_outstanding_and_resumes[1]: the stop left no work outstanding (6000 < 6000 relationships; the load finished before SIGTERM)
run_1.follow_on: 20 failures after it: 15 "query log did not become quiescent", 3 "an unexpected query was left open" (the harness graph observation), 2 "graph observation exceeds byte bound", looking like a cascade of that first failure

run_2.failure: test_s5_stream_stops_when_an_edge_loader_is_lost_and_resumes[1]: the CLI refused to start because the killed loader's consumer-group member had not yet expired ("waiting for member(s) to expire ... nothing was started")

diagnosis.a_graceful_stop_race: test workload race. In run 1 the relationship writes lasted 1.55 s (68 write queries); the first SIGTERM event landed 1.46 s after the first write and 0.09 s before the last (about 94% done), so the graceful stop drained the rest and 6000 of 6000 relationships existed (assertion "stop must have left work outstanding"). Cause: the test published all three relationship topics (about a second) before it began watching for work in flight, while the loaders were already writing; an idle host (NVMe-backed user stack, imdb-c7b4 containers stopped) shortens the window further.
diagnosis.b_edge_loader_lost: not a product defect and not the CLI refusing wrongly: the CLI waits session.timeout.ms + 5 s (about 50 s) for the killed loader's group member to expire before starting, which is the designed safety wait. The test's resume assertions were already true (the first run had written the whole graph before the kill, so "resumes to the exact graph" and "offsets at the ends" held at once) and it SIGTERMed the second CLI while it was still in that wait, giving exit 1 "nothing was started". Same root cause as (a): nothing was left outstanding.
diagnosis.c_cascade: yes. test_s5_stream_stops_gracefully[1] failed before its trailing clear(), leaving 2,006 nodes and 6,000 relationships in the shared scratch database. The next whole-database graph observation (test_s5_planned_bulk_fails_closed...[0],[1]) crossed the 2 MB byte bound and raised mid-iteration; the abandoned result left a started-but-never-completed query in Neo4j's query log. Neo4j never logs an end for it, so declare_open_writes rejected it ("an unexpected query was left open: MATCH (a)-[r]->(b)..." x3) and every later strict query_window.capture (all tests from test_service_lease_stream onward that use one) waited 30 s for a quiescence that cannot arrive (15 TimeoutErrors). 20 follow-on failures after the one root failure; independent tests after it could not run their real assertions.
